items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the multiple dwelling law and the limited liability company law, in relation to liability and penalties for illegal conversion
items.lawCode: Add §170-b, Mult Dwell L; amd §702, Lim Lil L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6693

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the multiple dwelling law and the
limited liability company law, in relation to liability and penalties
for illegal conversion

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To penalize Limited Liability Companies (LLC) that illegally convert
real property by authorizing the dissolution of the LLC by the Supreme
Court.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one of the bill would add a new Section 170-b to the Multiple
Dwelling Law to define "illegal conversion" as a change in the
structural parts or existing facilities of a building, including but
not limited to the subdivision of rooms, or erection or demolition of
walls, or the moving or any building from one location or position to
another, in violation of any state or local law, ordinance , code or
rule or regulation relating to real property, buildings or multiple
dwellings. In addition, the Attorney General would be authorized,
where an illegal conversion is undertaken or authorized by an LLC to
apply to the Supreme Court in the County in which the illegal
conversion lies for a judicially decreed dissolution of the LLC.

Section 2 of the bill would add a new Subdivision 2 to the Limited
Liability Corporation Law to provide for the corresponding authority
of the Court to dissolve an LLC where it is found to have violated the
new Section 170-b of the Multiple Dwelling Law relating to illegal
conversions.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This State has seen firsthand the tragedies that come out of illegally
converted homes. Our citizens have died as a result of fires tearing
through illegally converted homes which have been constructed in a
manner which ignore building safety codes and do not provide means for
egress in an emergency. Illegal conversions have also threatened our
local businesses that operate on the ground floors of mixed use
buildings, on some occasions facing ceiling collapse due to structural
stress arising out of illegal conversions on higher floors.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

 None to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

This State has seen firsthand the tragedies that come out of illegally
converted homes. Our citizens have died as a result of fires tearing
through illegally converted homes which have been constructed in a
manner which ignore building safety codes and do not provide means for
egress in an emergency. Illegal conversions have also threatened our
